records.claimSummary: In the internal stage the flag is on
records.bindingReason: For customer accounts the flag is off in the internal stage, so an unscoped 'flag is on' is false.

records.claimSummary: The internal stage lasts one working day
records.conditionSummary: usually; the guide sets no minimum
records.mustConvey: typical, not a minimum (no minimum set)
records.bindingReason: Read without 'usually / no minimum', it becomes a required one-day minimum, which the guide explicitly does not set.

records.claimSummary: During canary the flag is on for 5% of traffic
records.conditionSummary: 5% of requests chosen at random per request, not per user
records.bindingReason: Read as 5% of users, it misdescribes who sees the change (any user can hit flagged requests).
records.notes: u1_n4 says 'chosen randomly per request' but drops 'rather than per user'; judged recognisable.

records.claimSummary: The flag stays in canary at 5%
records.bindingReason: A canary shorter than 30 minutes violates the rule, so the canary step without the bound misleads on when it may end.

records.claimSummary: Canary must stay at 5% for at least 30 minutes
records.conditionSummary: raising the percentage by hand restarts the measurement window
records.bindingReason: The 30-minute rule stays true; the restart is an added consequence to know.

records.claimSummary: A flag advances from canary to general availability
records.conditionSummary: only when the automated metrics check passes; if it fails the flag stays in canary
records.mustConvey: only if automated metrics check passes
records.bindingReason: A flag whose check fails does not advance, so an unconditioned 'advances to GA' is false for it.
records.notes: The arrow u1_n5->u1_n7 is labelled 'if check passes'; arrow labels are not nodes, so not counted as a carrier. u1_n7/u1_n8 describe GA itself, not the advance, so are not claim cards.

records.claimSummary: Every flag must have a kill switch that turns it off
records.bindingReason: A kill switch slower than 1 minute does not meet the requirement, so dropping the bound makes the rule misleading.
records.notes: g2 takeaway and u2_a1 say 'rapid' only; not counted as carriers.

records.claimSummary: After internal, the rollout enters canary, exposing a small share of real traffic
records.conditionSummary: a flag cannot enter canary without a kill switch tested in staging and recorded in the rollout tool
records.mustConvey: tested kill switch required before canary
records.bindingReason: A flag without a tested kill switch cannot enter canary, so the stage sequence as stated is false for it.
records.notes: The frame-to-frame arrow g1->g2 is labelled 'kill switch tested before canary', which conveys the link at group level but does not join the cards to a carrier directly and is not g1's label/takeaway; judged separated. A scorer that credits group arrow labels would call this linked.

records.claimSummary: Turning a flag off is always safe
records.conditionSummary: turning it back on restarts the rollout from the internal stage
records.bindingReason: Turning off remains safe; the restart is a cost of re-enabling.

records.claimSummary: While the flag ramps up, the owner watches the error dashboard
records.conditionSummary: keeps watching until the flag has been at 100% for one hour
records.bindingReason: Read alone, watching stops when ramp-up ends at 100%; the rule requires another hour, so the claim misleads on the end point.

records.claimSummary: A flag is removed from the code
records.conditionSummary: after it has been fully on for 30 days
records.bindingReason: A flag fully on for fewer than 30 days is not yet removed, so the bare claim is false for it.
records.notes: u3_n5 ('Flag removed from code') states the claim without the bound; it is not directly linked to u3_n1/u3_n2, but frame g3 takeaway conveys 30 days.

records.claimSummary: The guide explains how a flag goes from off to fully on
records.conditionSummary: does not cover experiments, which follow their own process
records.bindingReason: The guide still explains flag rollout; excluding experiments is a scope note that must appear somewhere.
records.notes: All in frame g0, whose takeaway doesn't mention experiments; no arrow joins claim cards and carriers.

notes: Labelled against source v1 (packet units). No records for causes/rationale (u15 short canaries, u26 dashboard side-by-side, u31 old flags), chronology/records (u11, u19, u29), or examples. u17 comparison window (previous 7 days) treated as a detail of the check, not a limit on a claim. u23 (anyone may use kill switch) judged unconditioned. GA steps 25/50/100 (u10) are content, not a condition.
